input.summary:
P5 barn aisle and stalls now adds only the four hanging lanterns at y5 (4 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette).
The y1 stall fit-out and the y2 partition tops were removed because Shell B already builds those cells; the legend keeps only L.
./make.sh writes build.nbt with this part clean; the aisle gates are still closed, which is shell_b.mjs's to fix.
left: The aisle gates at (63,1,11), (63,1,13), (66,1,11) and (66,1,13) are built closed (open:false) by Shell B's barn stall fit-out, but the plan wants them open with the aisle clear at z11 and z13. The fix belongs in parts/shell_b.mjs (its owner); this part cannot change them because earlier parts are locked.
The z12 stall partitions are plain spruce_fence with no east/west connection states; the room intended east/west true. Minor, same owner as the gates.

Not reproduced: the first make.sh run reported the y2 partition tops as this part's placed writes, but later runs show Shell B owns those cells. I did not edit shell_b.mjs, so the cause is unexplained; the current build is clean for this part.

waste.what: Worked out which earlier part owned each of the refused cells by dumping the grid cell by cell with a one-off node script, then compared block states by eye.
waste.cost: one dump script over 6 x 7 x 6 cells, two extra full make.sh runs to confirm
waste.tool: runParts' refusal line and parts-report.json should name the owning part and print both block states for every refused cell (refusedAt is capped at 8 entries); MCD_PARTS_CELLS exists but is undocumented and needs a manual lookup.

waste.what: The refusal report prints block ids only, so the gate conflict (open:true wanted, open:false built) and the fence east/west state mismatch were invisible until I read states from the grid.
waste.cost: one extra grid dump and a manual comparison
waste.tool: a state-aware refusal line, or a lint (mcd conflicts <part>) that compares a part's layers() text against the cells earlier parts own, flagging redundant writes and state-only conflicts before any build.

waste.what: Recognised by hand, from the plan's stall rows, that the stall fit-out was written twice (Shell B and this room part); I only found the y2 overlap on the second run.
waste.cost: two full make.sh runs; one edit round wasted on the y1 layer before the y2 overlap showed
waste.tool: a dry run (runParts with no writes) that lists every cross-part overlap in one pass, or an owner map in plan.md, so duplicated fit-out is caught at plan time.

companions.task: Hang the four barn aisle gates open (open:true, facing outward on the aisle) and set the z12 stall partitions' east/west connections in the stall fit-out, which belongs to Shell B.
